events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1: The driver's own brief concedes the unexempted off-route segment: 5.23 km driven against 1.08 km optimal, +4.15 km, up to 1989 m off route (F4), with the trip running 10.2 km against 7.2 km optimal, +3.0 km (F2) — that is the RD-1 breach, and nothing in the record excuses it. [F4 F2] [RD-1]
→ D2 (concedes): Agreed and adopted: the chat contains no rider route authorisation at all before the 09:04 segment (F8, F9, F10), so the segment is not excused by consent under RD-5. [F8 F9 F10] [RD-5]
→ D3 (concedes): Agreed: the driver's 'the GPS rerouted' statement (F11) is a post-trip claim contradicted by the complete, timestamped chat (F10) and by the absence of any incident (F14), so it cannot be consent or reasonable cause. [F11 F10 F14] [RD-5 RD-4]
→ D4 (concedes): Agreed that RD-4 does not exempt the segment: no incident was recorded (F14) and the corridor shows only band 3, 20–29 km/h (F12, F13), which is not even the band 1/2 evidence RD-4(b) treats as corroborative. [F14 F12 F13] [RD-4]
→ D5: D5 mis-states RD-2: the refund is Σ(unexempted extra km) × the trip's per-km rate, and the segment extra is 4.15 km (F4) at $1.4100/km (F5), i.e. $5.85, so my $7.04 request is already generous — it adopts the fare record's weaker 4.99 km excess-distance figure (F5) rather than the larger segment figure. [F4 F5 F7] [RD-2]
→ D6: RD-6 is not offered as proof of the deviation — the deviation is proved by F4 and F2 — it is offered only as the additional flag_account step, and the driver's one upheld dispute plus 3 disputes in 90 days (F17) supplies the 'repeated' limb once this case is upheld. [F17 F4 F2] [RD-6]
→ D7: D7 cuts the driver's way only on the uncovered tail (F1), not on the finding that matters: the segment 09:04–09:14 sits inside the covered stretch and is fully measured in F4, and any mileage outside it is not being claimed by me. [F1 F4] [RD-1]
→ D8 (concedes): Agreed the profile facts decide nothing on liability (F16, F17); they are cited only for the RD-6 add-on, which needs the route finding to be established first. [F16 F17] [RD-6]

[F4 F10 F14 F17] [RD-2 RD-1 RD-6]
Revised ask: refund_partial $7.04

events.body:
The rider complains the driver took a different way on a metered RydeTAXI trip (estimate 7.2 km, meter 12 km) and wants the extra distance back [F2][F7][RD-1]. The covered trace shows one off-route segment 09:04–09:14 driving 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, +4.15 km and up to 1989 m off route [F4], which on its face is an unexplained breach of the shortest-and-most-direct duty [F4][RD-1].

Nothing exempts that segment. The complete, fully timestamped chat [F10] contains only the rider's 08:47 pickup note about waiting outside Beach Station with a black backpack [F8] and the driver's 08:48 "on my way" note [F9]; no rider message before 09:04 agrees to any route change [F8][F9][RD-5], and a driver's post-trip claim is not consent [F11][RD-5]. The traffic record gives no reasonable cause: no incident near the route in the window [F14], and only speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway [F12][F13], which is not band 1/2 and is at most corroborative anyway [RD-4]. Fair weather removes any weather excuse [F15][RD-4]. So the segment counts as unexempted [F4][RD-2].

The refund therefore belongs on the meter: RydeTAXI bills by distance unit, so extra kilometres enter the fare directly [F7][RD-2]. But the amount cannot be fixed on this record. The trace does not cover the whole trip — the last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off [F1] — and the fare record bills 12.17 km ($17.16 ÷ $1.4100/km) [F7] while the GPS total is 10.2 km [F2], an unattributed 1.97 km gap, in addition to the 4.99 km excess-billing fact [F5] which RD-2 refuses to refund where the mileage is not attributed to a segment [F5][F2][F7][RD-2]. The covered-segment figure (4.15 km × $1.4100/km ≈ $5.85) rests only on F4 while the uncovered stretch is unmeasured [F1], so neither $7.04 [F5] nor $5.85 is settled by the record [F1][F4][RD-2]. Per the no-gap rule, missing evidence is not read in either side's favour, so the case goes to a person.

The RD-6 add-on is not triggered: the driver profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 d, none route-related [F17], so even a finding against him would not make this "repeated" enough to send his account to review, and profile facts cannot decide the deviation itself [F17][RD-6]. The rider's own clean profile is likewise only context [F16][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F8][F9], the driver's statement [F11] and the complaint; they contain only a pickup note, an ETA note, a route-justification claim and a fare grievance — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

what_would_change: Had the trace left the quoted route by more than 200 m for a stretch adding at least 0.2 km, RD-1 would apply and the extra kilometres would be weighed.

claims.assertion: The trip drove one off-route segment (09:04–09:14) covering 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.15 km and straying up to 1,989 m from the optimal route — an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route.

No rider message before the segment agrees to any reroute: the only pre-segment rider messages are about waiting outside Beach Station with a black backpack; the driver's own statement that 'it rerouted' was written after the trip and is a claim, not a consent.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites G11 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: No traffic justification exists: no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and the only speed bands are band 3 (20–29 km/h), not severe congestion, so RD-4 never engages and the segment stays unexempted.
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra distance entered the fare directly: the meter bills 12.17 km against a 7.2 km estimate, $17.16 distance fare at $1.41/km, extra km billed at $1.41/km.

The excess-distance refund computable from the fare record is $7.04 (4.99 km × $1.4100/km), and the driver's written statement that the fare is simply 'what the meter showed' does not answer why the meter ran 4.97 km long.
The driver already has one upheld dispute in the last 90 days, so a finding against him here makes this a repeated route-related breach and warrants sending his account to Ryde for review.

weaknesses: The GPS trace does not cover the whole trip (last sample 4 min before 09:20:45), so the tail of the trip is not on record and the driver can argue the uncovered stretch included unavoidable routing (F1).

Aggregate GPS distance is 10.2 km (F2) while the fare record bills 12.17 km (F7); the driver will point at this 1.97 km gap to argue the off-route segment figure (F4) understates or mis-matches the billed distance, and RD-2 expressly refuses mileage differences not attributed to any segment.

The driver's statement that 'the GPS rerouted' me (F11) may invite a RD-4 reasonable-cause reading, and speed bands 3 on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway (F12, F13) could be spun as congestion even though RD-4(b) alone does not exempt a segment.
The rider's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F16), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of unsuccessful claims.
Waiting time is $0.00 (F7), so no waiting-fee angle exists; any refund must come from mileage only.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 09:04–09:14, in which 5.23 km were driven where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.15 km and reaching up to 1989 m from the optimal route (F4); the trip as a whole ran 10.2 km against an optimal 7.2 km, +3.0 km (F2).

No rider message before the segment at 09:04 agrees to any route change: the only rider message is the 08:47 pickup note about waiting outside Beach Station with a black backpack (F8), and the only driver message is the 08:48 'on my way' note (F9); there is no route authorisation in the chat at all (F10).

The driver's written statement that 'the GPS rerouted' (F11) is a post-trip claim, not rider consent, and it is contradicted by the system records: the chat shows no reroute agreement (F10) and the traffic records show no incident in the window (F14).

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window (F14), and the only band records on the corridor are speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Eu Tong Sen Street and Sentosa Gateway, which is not band 1 or 2 severe congestion and in any event is corroborative only (F12, F13); so the RD-4 reasonable-cause exception does not exempt the segment.

This is a metered RydeTAXI trip charged $28.97 with distance $17.16 for 12.17 km at $1.41/km (F7) and an excess-distance component of 4.99 km = $7.04 (F5); on RD-2 the refund exposure is confined to the unexempted segment's extra kilometres and must be computed only from the segment figures, not from the whole excess billing.

The driver has one previously upheld dispute in 90 days (F17), which on RD-6 is capable only of adding a flag_account referral, never of establishing the deviation itself; the record shows no upheld route deviation against this driver (F17).

The GPS trace does not cover the whole trip — the last sample is 4 minutes before the 09:20:45 drop-off (F1) — so the mileage outside the covered stretch is not on record and cannot be attributed to the driver as deviation; the segment finding must rest on F4 alone.

The rider's own account is 997 days old with a 5.0 rating and no upheld dispute (F16), and the driver's is 1566 days old with 677 trips in 90 days and a 4.55 rating (F17); profile facts cannot decide the route finding in either direction.

weaknesses: The off-route segment F4 is real and large — 5.23 km driven against 1.08 km optimal, +4.15 km, up to 1989 m off the optimal route — and the driver has no rider message consenting to it (F10), so an RD-2 finding against the client is likely on that segment.

D5 mis-states RD-2: the refund is Σ(unexempted extra km) × the trip's per-km rate, and the segment extra is 4.15 km (F4) at $1.4100/km (F5), i.e. $5.85, so my $7.04 request is already generous — it adopts the fare record's weaker 4.99 km excess-distance figure (F5) rather than the larger segment figure.

The driver's request for no_action is therefore untenable: with the segment unexempted (F4), no consent (F10) and no traffic cause (F14), RD-2 requires a partial refund of at least $5.85 and supports the $7.04 claimed, plus a flag_account referral under RD-6 (F17).
